text: When metal is microwaved, the electric field from the radiation causes free electrons in the metal to move about randomly. This creates a voltage difference between different parts of the metal. If the metal has sharp edges or thin points, like crinkled foil, the electric field becomes highly concentrated there. This allows the energy to jump from one point to another in the air, or to ground, as a spark. This is an electrical discharge, a little lightning bolt. Often, the metal is thin and the energy is too high for the metal to handle so it heats up very quickly, can melt and start burning.
